evidence_items.locator: Privacy questions, 'Who has access to my chats, and how does human review improve Gemini for everyone?'
evidence_items.explanation: Google describes reviewers assessing users' nonpublic conversations and supplying improvements used by its models. The same FAQ explicitly includes generative-model training among uses of saved activity when Keep Activity is enabled; e2 establishes the default-participation policy.

evidence_items.publisher: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society
evidence_items.locator: Table 1 and its explanatory caption, page 1470
evidence_items.explanation: Table 1 records both default training on chat inputs and an opt-out mechanism for Google. This independent policy analysis corroborates that training participation does not require an affirmative opt-in, although it does not inspect individual training datasets.

evidence_items.locator: Section 'Control your data with new settings'
evidence_items.explanation: Google provides an opt-out and temporary conversations excluded from training. This limits any interpretation that every user's information must be used or that an exercised objection is necessarily ignored.

unresolved_gaps: The cited records do not establish that Google trained on a particular person's information after that person exercised an applicable opt-out.
The policy study examines disclosed practices, not underlying training datasets.
